slides.headline: THE CEO OF OPENAI JUST KILLED THE 4-DAY WORKWEEK
slides.subline: AND HIS REASON WILL INFURIATE YOU

slides.headline: SAM ALTMAN SAID FORGET THE 4-DAY WEEK
slides.body: On July 28, Altman told Ti Morse on the Relentless podcast that the shorter workweek will never happen at mass scale. His exact words: "I don't expect AI to change that." He argues every time humans get better tools, they just raise their expectations to match

slides.headline: HE CALLED YOU SECRETLY HAPPY
slides.body: Altman said people are "very focused on how they're doing relative to other people." His prediction: even after AI gets smarter than all of us, "we're still going to complain about it, but secretly we're going to be happy." He claims we already have more free time and a better quality of life than any other point in history

slides.headline: BERNIE SANDERS FIRED BACK
slides.body: On the Joe Rogan Experience, Sanders said time saved by AI should go back to workers, not get filled with extra tasks. The UK, France, Japan, and Germany are already testing four-day workweeks. Meanwhile, the people already replaced by AI "now work no hours each week"

slides.headline: 4 COUNTRIES ALREADY TESTED SHORTER WEEKS
slides.body: You're paying your team for 40 hours but half goes to tasks AI handles in minutes. The UK, France, Japan, and Germany already tested shorter weeks without losing output. Your business can do the same without a government program or a single new hire

slides.headline: THIS FIGHT IS JUST STARTING
slides.body: Altman won't be the last CEO to tell you to keep grinding. Follow @yaffeai so you see who says it next. Send this to the friend who hates their 9-to-5 but hasn't done anything about it

hook_tournament.why: KILLED + INFURIATE YOU is a double emotional gut-punch — 'killed' makes it feel like something was taken from me, and 'infuriate' tells me my anger is the correct response before I've even read it. [6] is close but 'the guy building AI says you'll work more' spreads its energy across two ideas; [7] lands one clean blow and the subline amplifies it instead of restating it.
